veranderings.rede: The nearest antecedent of 'Dit' is 'n oopmyn' (the hole), but the sentence is about the method, oopmynbou.

veranderings.voor: maak die landskap oor 'n groot gebied stukkend
veranderings.na: beskadig die landskap oor 'n groot gebied
veranderings.rede: 'Stukkend maak' is used for objects and sounds childish for a landscape; 'beskadig' is grade-appropriate and keeps the meaning.
'Oop uitgegrawe' is awkward; 'van bo af' carries the same open-pit sense and echoes the lesson's own wording for oopmynbou.
The two adverbs 'dieper' and 'verder' sit apart and read clumsily; joining them reads naturally with the same meaning.

veranderings.voor: 'n diep opening in die grond wat dikwels reguit af loop
veranderings.na: 'n diep opening wat dikwels reguit af in die grond loop
veranderings.rede: 'Wat' directly follows 'die grond', so it can be read as the ground running straight down; moving 'in die grond' makes it refer to the opening, and 'dikwels reguit af' stays intact.

veranderings.na: Watter metode gebruik word, hang af van
veranderings.rede: 'Die metode' has no clear referent after two methods; the sentence means the choice of method depends on depth.

veranderings.na: moet vir 'n oopmyn eers verwyder word
veranderings.rede: The lesson defines an oopmyn as the hole itself, and a hole cannot remove soil; the passive keeps the meaning without that mismatch.

beskerm_bedenkings.rede: The reason given refers to Grade 7 Life Orientation lessons, not this lesson; the word is right to keep here (it sits in the decided definition of ondergrondse mynbou and in the study text), but the reason does not explain this lesson's use.
